newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Metro enters luxury cruise business.
newsitem.headline: Metro enters luxury cruise business.

text.p: Retailer Metro Holdings said on Friday it will diversify into the luxury cruise ship business, committing about Singapore $88.25 million to purchase a ship.
It said in a statement that Metro's entry into the leisure and cruise business would provide an opportunity to broaden assets and earnings base.
The retailing group has also diversified into properties, developing one of Singapore's largest shopping centres in the prime Orchard Road area, and is building a hotel in Cairns, Australia.
Metro said the Asia-Pacific cruise market was one of the fastest growing markets driven by rising living standards and affluence.
Metro will buy the 30,440-tonne SS Meridian, with a passenger capacity of 1,398, from Fourth Transoceanic Shipping Co Ltd.
The acquisition will be funded by internal sources and external borrowing, it said.
The statement said the purchase was not expected to have any material impact on the group's earnings per share and net tangible assets per share for the year ending March 31.
Metro shares were up six cents at S$4.74 at midday on Friday.
